title: Best Stand Mixers UK
short: Seven stand mixers compared on how they coped when filled to maximum dough capacity, plus noise, shake and everyday mixing and whisking.
intro: A stand mixer's real test is how it copes when pushed, not how it looks on the worktop. This guide is based on Expert Reviews' tested roundup, where each mixer was filled to maximum dough capacity to check for overheating, noise and shake, then used with its standard attachments for whipping egg whites, cake batter and frosting, timed with consistent volumes. The guide is from September 2024, so prices are as reviewed.

products.name: kMix KMX754
products.best_for: Buyers who want solid performance and large capacity at a budget price
products.key_spec: 1,000W, 5L glass bowl, holds 2.72kg cake mixture or 1.35kg bread dough, variable speed
products.summary: Expert Reviews found one of the few stand mixers under £400 that can stand up to or outperform pricier rivals. Its extra-large capacity holds enough for a couple of loaves or several Victoria sponges, and even filled to capacity the motor didn't overheat, though it gets a little shaky making bread dough and isn't the best dough kneader.

specs.Attachments: K beater, wire whisk, dough hook, splash guard

pros: Solid performance at a budget price
Extra-large capacity
Motor doesn't overheat when filled to capacity
Looks great on the counter
cons: Gets a little shaky making bread dough

products.name: SMF03 Retro Stand Mixer
products.best_for: Bakers who want beautiful design and top mixing ability for cakes and meringues
products.key_spec: 800W, 4.8L, ten speeds, glossy retro design in cream, red or black
products.summary: Expert Reviews found a stand mixer that's not just a pretty face: it whipped a double helping of Victoria sponge batter in seconds and made easy work of meringue egg whites. Pushed to its bread dough capacity it struggled towards the end of kneading and the motor's safety mechanism kicked in to stop overheating, so heavy daily bread bakers may want a bigger motor.
pros: Beautiful, sleek retro design
Top mixing ability for sponge batter and egg whites
cons: Motor struggles when kneading bread at full capacity

products.name: Artisan 5KSM175PS
products.best_for: Well-seasoned or aspiring bakers who want extra attachments and a second bowl
products.key_spec: 300W, 4.8L plus an additional 3L bowl, ten speeds, four attachments
products.summary: Expert Reviews found speedy, thorough mixing, blending mixtures to perfection in seconds across ten speeds from lightly whipping egg whites to vigorous kneading. Four sturdy attachments and an extra bowl will see you through tough bakes, and once you count the additional space, power, attachments and bowl, the price jump over a classic model doesn't seem outrageous, though it's a little pricey and rather large.
pros: Speedy, thorough mixing
Four sturdy attachments and a second bowl included
Ten speeds cover everything from whipping to kneading

products.name: Titanium Chef Patissier XL
products.best_for: Serious bakers who want in-bowl weighing, warming and a huge capacity
products.key_spec: 1,400W, 7L warming bowl plus 5L classic bowl, in-bowl weighing and warming, preset programmes, dishwasher-safe
products.summary: Expert Reviews found an all-in-one baking machine that does everything a traditional mixer does, plus in-bowl weighing and warming so you can weigh, mix and prove dough in one bowl, or melt chocolate and butter and make Swiss meringue. The digital screen is a nice touch though it can lag, and the price is best justified for keen bakers rather than casual ones.
pros: Wide range of features and top performance
Weighs, mixes and proves in one bowl
Large 7L warming bowl and 5L classic bowl included
Dishwasher-safe bowls and attachments
cons: Not for casual home bakers, expensive
Digital screen can lag at times

products.name: Artisan 5.6L Bowl Lift
products.best_for: Home cooks who mix large quantities of stiff dough or make pizza regularly
products.key_spec: 325W, 5.6L, 11 speeds including half speed, bowl-lift design, compatible with 15 attachments
products.summary: Expert Reviews filled it to maximum capacity with cookie batter, pizza dough and egg whites and were impressed: it can hold 0.5kg of dry flour, making 3.7kg of dough or 11 small pizzas. Unlike many tilt-head mixers tested, the bowl lift kept cool under pressure with minimal shaking and rattling, and a half speed helps start flour-heavy mixtures, though it's very pricey.
pros: Excellent with large quantities of tougher doughs
Kept its cool at capacity, minimal shaking and rattling
Half speed useful for folding and flour-heavy starts
Four colours and 15 compatible attachments

products.name: Classic K45SS
products.best_for: Casual bakers who want a compact KitchenAid for cakes and light mixing
products.summary: Expert Reviews found the smaller of KitchenAid's two popular home mixers pretty good, powerful enough for home baking, though tough jobs like kneading dough are a struggle for the motor, so daily bread bakers should choose something stronger. It doesn't come with a splash guard, which should be standard at this price, and other models offer dramatically more power for similar money.
pros: Compact mixer for casual baking
Powerful enough for typical home baking such as GBBO-style cakes
cons: Lacks high-end power, struggles kneading dough
Other models offer far more power for similar money

products.name: Titanium Chef Baker
products.best_for: Bakers who want to weigh ingredients straight into the bowl and use attachments
products.key_spec: 1,000W, 5L, ten speeds, built-in digital scales and timer, attachment hub
products.summary: Expert Reviews found the built-in digital scales a huge benefit, saving time and washing up, and they double as a timer for precise mixing and kneading. It's an excellent premium mixer with a beefy 1,000W motor and a 5L bowl holding up to 12 eggs, 1.3kg of dough or 2kg of cake batter, plus an attachment hub for extras like a lasagne roller, mincer and blender, though it isn't as sleek as its rivals.
pros: Built-in digital scales and timer
Beefy 1,000W motor
Attachment hub for a lasagne roller, mincer and blender
Large capacity for most home baking
cons: Isn't quite as sleek as its rivals

guide.a: A tilt-head mixer, like most here, tilts back for access and suits cakes and light dough. A bowl-lift mixer, like the KitchenAid Artisan 5.6L, raises the bowl to the beater and copes better with stiff dough and big batches. Expert Reviews found the bowl-lift stayed cooler with far less shaking than many tilt-heads when full.

guide.q: How much power do I need?
guide.a: Watts aren't everything: KitchenAid's 300W Artisan mixed quickly and thoroughly in testing, while Kenwood's 1,000-1,400W models offer more muscle for heavy kneading. If you knead bread most days, choose a bigger motor, since the Smeg and KitchenAid Classic here both struggled at full dough capacity.

guide.q: Is it worth paying for built-in scales or warming?
guide.a: For keen bakers, yes: the Kenwood Titanium Chef Baker's scales let you weigh straight into the bowl and double as a timer, and the Chef Patissier XL adds in-bowl warming for proving dough and melting chocolate. For casual bakers, a simpler mixer like the Kenwood kMix does the everyday jobs for much less.

Most mixers include a dough hook, balloon whisk and a beater. Check extras such as a splash guard (missing on the KitchenAid Classic here), a second bowl (included with the Artisan 5KSM175PS) and whether the mixer has an attachment hub for extras like a mincer or pasta roller, as Kenwood models do.
